senses.title: Belonging to another country
senses.definition: belonging to or connected with a country that is not yours
senses.definitionCN: 属于或关于他国的
senses.example: They import foreign cars.
senses.exampleCN: 他们进口外国汽车。
senses.why: The core image is something standing beyond your own border.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是立于国境之外的东西。

senses.title: Coming from outside a place or body
senses.definition: entering a place or body from outside where it does not belong
senses.definitionCN: 从外部进入某个地方或身体、并不属于那里
senses.example: A foreign body in the eye hurts.
senses.exampleCN: 眼睛里的异物很疼。
senses.why: The border is not only national; any boundary makes an inside and a foreign outside.
senses.whyCN: 边界不只在国与国之间，任何界线都会分出内与外。

senses.title: Strange and unfamiliar
senses.definition: strange, unfamiliar, or not belonging in a situation
senses.definitionCN: 奇怪、不熟悉或与处境格格不入
senses.example: Kindness was foreign to him.
senses.exampleCN: 他对善良感到陌生。
senses.why: What lies outside your experience feels as far as another country.
senses.whyCN: 经验之外的东西，如同异国一样遥远。

intro.en: Foreign comes through French from Latin words about doors and thresholds.
intro.cn: foreign 经法语来自拉丁语中与门、门槛有关的词。

items.en: Latin foris meant outside, out of doors, beyond the threshold.
items.cn: 拉丁语 foris 意为在外、门外、门槛之外。

items.en: Medieval Latin foraneus meant lying outside, applied to towns beyond one's own.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 foraneus 意为处于外部，用于指自己属地之外的城镇。

items.en: Old French forain meant outside, especially outside the law or the community.
items.cn: 古法语 forain 意为外面的，尤指法律或共同体之外。

items.en: Middle English took forein or strange in law, commerce and travel.
items.cn: 中古英语吸收 forein，用于法律、商业与旅行语境。

items.en: Modern English fixed the national sense and added the metaphorical unfamiliar sense.
items.cn: 现代英语确立国家义项，并增加比喻性的陌生义。

note.en: Foreign has a tight family from the same Latin door.
note.cn: foreign 的词族都出自同一个拉丁「门」。

senses.title: The working of a machine or system
senses.definition: the way in which a device, plant or system performs its function
senses.definitionCN: 装置、工厂或系统发挥功能的方式
senses.example: The pump's operation is monitored from a control room.
senses.exampleCN: 泵的运转由控制室监控。
senses.why: The word rests on a Latin verb meaning to work, so the working of a system is its most literal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在拉丁语「工作」动词之上，因此系统的运转是它最字面的义项。

senses.title: The act of making a device work
senses.definition: the act of running or controlling a machine by hand or by control
senses.definitionCN: 用手或控制装置使机器运行的动作
senses.example: Operation of the crane requires two trained hands.
senses.exampleCN: 操作这台吊车需要两名受过训练的人。
senses.why: Doing the work and making something else work are two sides of one verb, so the act of driving a machine took the same noun.
senses.whyCN: 自己干活与让别的东西干活是同一个动词的两面，因此驱动机器的动作也用了这个名词。

senses.title: A surgical treatment
senses.definition: a treatment in which a surgeon cuts into or enters the body to repair it
senses.definitionCN: 外科医生切开或进入体内进行修补的治疗
senses.example: The operation on her knee lasted two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 她膝盖的手术持续了两个小时。
senses.why: Surgery is work done on a body, so medicine used the general noun for work and it became the everyday word for an intervention.
senses.whyCN: 手术是对身体所做的工作，因此医学用这个泛指「工作」的名词，它后来成了介入治疗的日常说法。

senses.title: A planned military action
senses.definition: an organized movement of forces with a set aim, usually given a name
senses.definitionCN: 有明确目标、通常有代号的部队组织行动
senses.example: The rescue operation began at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 救援行动在黎明开始。
senses.why: Military staffs speak of work done by combined forces as one operation, and the sense spread to any coordinated action.
senses.whyCN: 军事参谋把多支部队合力完成的工作称为一次行动，这个义项后来扩展到任何协同行动。

senses.title: The everyday activities of a business
senses.definition: the routine activities by which a company or institution keeps running, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 公司或机构维持运转的日常活动，常用复数
senses.example: The firm moved its operations closer to the port.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司把业务迁到离港口更近的地方。
senses.why: A business is a set of workings, so its routine activities are called its operations rather than its plans.
senses.whyCN: 一家企业就是一组运转，因此它的日常活动被称为业务，而不是计划。

senses.title: A mathematical process
senses.definition: a rule applied to numbers or symbols to produce a new value
senses.definitionCN: 施于数字或符号以得出新值的规则
senses.example: Addition is the first operation children learn.
senses.exampleCN: 加法是孩子学的第一种运算。
senses.why: Mathematics treats each rule as work performed on symbols, which is the same idea of a working applied to numbers.
senses.whyCN: 数学把每条规则看作对符号所做的工作，这与「运转」是同一个意思，只是对象换成数字。

senses.title: A running business or unit
senses.definition: an enterprise or a distinct unit that is being run as a going concern
senses.definitionCN: 作为持续经营体运作的企业或独立单位
senses.example: The mine is a profitable operation.
senses.exampleCN: 这座矿是一个盈利的经营单位。
senses.why: Once a business is seen as something that works, the thing that works can itself be called an operation.
senses.whyCN: 一旦企业被看作在运转的东西，这个在运转的东西本身就可以被称为一个经营单位。

senses.title: An organized piece of work with a plan
senses.titleCN: 有组织的行动；专项行动
senses.definition: a coordinated piece of work, often large, carried out by a group toward one aim
senses.definitionCN: 由一群人朝同一目标实施的、常具规模的协同工作
senses.example: The cleanup operation involved three hundred volunteers.
senses.exampleCN: 这次清理行动动用了三百名志愿者。
senses.why: Any large piece of coordinated work can be called an operation, because it is work organized as one working whole.
senses.whyCN: 任何大规模协同工作都可称为一次行动，因为它被组织成一个整体的运作。

intro.en: Operation came through Old French from Latin operatio 'a working', built on operari 'to work' and opus 'work'. The origin of opus before Latin is unsettled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词经古法语来自拉丁语表示「工作」的名词，其基础为表示「工作」的动词与名词。名词词根在拉丁语之前的来源没有定论。年代均为约数。

items.en: Opus meant 'work, a piece of work, a task'. Its pre-Latin origin is not established, and the root sometimes proposed for it is a reconstruction, so source uncertain at that depth.
items.cn: opus 意为「工作、一件作品、任务」。其在拉丁语之前的来源未获证明，有时为它提出的词根属重构形式，故更深一层来源不确定。

items.en: Operari, a deponent verb, meant 'to work, to labour, to perform'.
items.cn: operari 是一个异态动词，意为「工作、劳作、施行」。

items.en: Operatio, from operari plus the noun suffix -io, named a working or the result of working.
items.cn: operatio 由 operari 加名词后缀 -io 构成，指工作这一动作或其结果。

items.en: Old French brought the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first for any action or effect.
items.cn: 古法语在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，最初指任何动作或效果。

items.en: From the seventeenth century surgery adopted the word for an intervention, and from the eighteenth military staffs used it for a named action.
items.cn: 十七世纪起外科把这个词用于介入治疗，十八世纪起军事参谋用它指有代号的行动。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin noun of work, plus one that only looks similar; group two holds words that overlap with it in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「工作」名词的词，外加一个仅形似的词；第二组是语义上与本词重叠的词。

entries.definition: To run a machine, to carry on business or to perform surgery; the noun names the working, the verb performs it.
entries.definitionCN: 指运转机器、开展业务或施行手术；名词指运转本身，动词指施行。

entries.definition: The person who runs a machine or a business, formed with the agent suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 用施动后缀构成，指操作机器或经营业务的人。

entries.definition: Co- 'together' plus the same verb: joint work, with no single unit of action.
entries.definitionCN: co-「共同」加同一动词：指共同工作，不指单个动作单元。

entries.definition: From orare 'to speak', not from opus: a formal speech, similar only in its ending.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 orare「说话」，而非 opus：指正式演说，仅词尾相似。

entries.definition: The branch of medicine and the procedure itself, with nothing about machines or business.
entries.definitionCN: 指外科这一学科及手术本身，与机器或业务无关。

entries.definition: The ordered steps of an action; it does not imply that anything is actually running.
entries.definitionCN: 指行动的有序步骤，并不表示事情真的在运转。

entries.definition: The proper role or capacity of a part; it names what something is for, not how it runs.
entries.definitionCN: 指某部件的应有作用或能力，说明它用于什么，而非如何运转。

entries.definition: A connected series of actions for one aim, often public or military; it stresses duration, not a single working.
entries.definitionCN: 为同一目标展开的系列行动，常为宣传或军事行动；强调持续时间，而非单次运作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: A Latin noun of work plus a noun suffix: the doing of work, and then any piece of work that is done.
normal.cn: 拉丁「工作」名词加名词后缀：先指干活，再指所干的任一件事。

normal.en: One root yields the verb to run, the person who runs, the adjective for running order and the noun for joint work.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出表示运转的动词、表示操作者的名词、表示运转状态的形容词，以及表示合作的名词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the settings: in operation, surgical operation, rescue operation, daily operations.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出场景：在运转中、外科手术、救援行动、日常业务。

normal.en: Hospitals, armies and mathematics all call their own kind of work by this one name.
normal.cn: 医院、军队与数学都把自己那类工作用同一个名称来称呼。

normal.en: A factory is said to be in operation, and later the factory itself is called an operation.
normal.cn: 工厂被说成处于运转中，后来工厂本身也被称为一个经营单位。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose gears keep turning while nobody watches.
abstract.cn: 想象一座钟的齿轮在无人注视时仍不停转动。

abstract.en: Picture a surgeon's hands as the only still thing in a room full of machines.
abstract.cn: 想象一屋子机器都在动，只有外科医生的手是静的。

abstract.en: Picture a column of figures that changes when one rule is applied.
abstract.cn: 想象一列数字在施加一条规则后整体改变。

examples.en: The plant has been in operation since the river was dammed.
examples.cn: 这座工厂自河流筑坝以来一直在运转。

examples.en: The peacekeeping operation was extended for another six months.
examples.cn: 维和行动又延长了六个月。

examples.en: Division is the operation most often done wrong under time pressure.
examples.cn: 除法是时间紧迫时最容易算错的一种运算。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「oper（工作）+ ation（名词）」——在工作、在运转 → 运转、操作、手术、行动、运算

root: 拉丁语「工作」名词派生出「工作、施行」的动词，再加后缀构成「工作、运作」的名词；名词词根更早的来源无定论，相关词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of working: a machine runs, a hand makes it run, a surgeon works on a body, an army works on an objective, a company works every day, a rule works on numbers, a working enterprise is itself a unit, and any coordinated effort is one operation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「工作」动作展开：机器运转、手使它运转、医生在身体上工作、军队对一个目标行动、公司每天运作、规则对数字起作用、运转中的企业本身成为一个单位，最后任何协同用力都算一次行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: gears turning under a lamp while a hand rests on the switch that keeps them turning.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯下齿轮转动，一只手按在使它们继续转动的开关上。

branches.en: RUNNING AND DRIVING: the working of a system and the act that keeps it working are one event seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 运转与驱动：系统的运转与使它运转的动作，是同一件事的两面。

branches.en: ON A BODY: surgery is work performed on flesh with tools.
branches.cn: 施于身体：手术是用工具在血肉上所做的工作。

branches.en: ON AN AIM: a named military action and any coordinated effort are work organized toward one end.
branches.cn: 对准目标：有代号的军事行动与任何协同工作，都是朝一个目标组织起来的劳动。

branches.en: THE WORKING UNIT: a company's daily business and the enterprise itself are the same working seen as activity and as thing.
branches.cn: 运转单位：公司的日常业务与企业本身，是同一个运转被看作活动与看作实体。

branches.en: ON SYMBOLS: arithmetic applies the same notion of work to numbers.
branches.cn: 施于符号：算术把同一个「工作」观念用在数字上。

intro.en: Operation is a Latin noun of work: a root noun for a task and a verb for doing it, with a suffix that turns the doing into a name.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示「工作」的拉丁名词：一个指任务的词根名词、一个指做这件事的动词，以及把「做」变成名称的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin opus and operari give operate, operator, operation and cooperation; the noun suffix marks the act or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「工作」的名词与动词衍生出运转、操作者与合作等词；名词后缀标记动作或其结果。

items.example: The root noun names the task itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根名词指任务本身。

items.example: The verb turns the task into activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把任务变成活动。

items.example: The suffix makes the activity a countable thing.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把活动变成可计数的东西。

items.example: English keeps both the activity and its result.
items.exampleCN: 英语兼指动作与其结果。

items.example: The suffix is the same one that builds many nouns of process.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀也构成许多表示过程的名词。

items.example: One verb covers machines, businesses and surgeons.
items.exampleCN: 一个动词兼指机器、企业与外科医生。

items.meaning: one who works a machine or business
items.meaningCN: 操作机器或经营业务的人
items.example: The agent suffix names the person at the controls.
items.exampleCN: 施动后缀指在控制台前的人。

items.example: The prefix makes the work shared.
items.exampleCN: 前缀使这份工作成为共享的。

items.meaningCN: 处于运转状态的；生效的
items.example: A rule becomes operative when it starts to apply.
items.exampleCN: 规则开始适用时便生效。

definition_zh: 院子；庭院；场地；（工厂等的）堆场；码
definition_en: an open area beside or around a building, an enclosed area used for work, or a unit of length equal to about ninety centimetres

scene: 雨停后，屋后的空地上积了一小滩水，孩子在栅栏边踩来踩去。 My father keeps his old bicycle in the yard behind the house.
sceneCN: 这里 yard 是「院子；庭院」（第 1 个义项：房屋旁边或四周的空地）；句意为父亲把旧自行车放在屋后的院子里。屋后矮栅栏围出的那块空地，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: The open ground by a house
senses.definition: a piece of open ground, often enclosed, beside or around a house or other building
senses.definitionCN: 房屋或其他建筑旁边或四周的一块空地，常用围墙围起
senses.example: My father keeps his old bicycle in the yard behind the house.
senses.exampleCN: 父亲把旧自行车放在屋后的院子里。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the root is an enclosed patch of ground, and the space fenced beside a dwelling is its most familiar form.
senses.whyCN: 词根最早的意思就是围起来的一块地，房屋旁边 fencing 出来的那块空间正是它最常见的样子。

senses.title: The working ground
senses.definition: an enclosed area used for a particular kind of work, such as storing goods, building ships, or sorting railway cars
senses.definitionCN: 为某种工作而围起来的场地，如堆放货物、造船或调度车辆
senses.example: Trucks waited in line outside the railway yard all night.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车在铁路调车场外排了一整夜。
senses.why: Once ground is set aside and fenced, it can be filled with any work, so the enclosed patch shifts from home to industry.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把地圈起来围住，就可以用它做任何活计，于是围地这个词从家宅挪到了工业里。

senses.title: The long measure
senses.definition: a unit of length used in Britain and America, equal to three feet or about ninety centimetres
senses.definitionCN: 英美使用的长度单位，合三英尺，约九十厘米
senses.example: The dress needs two yards of blue cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 这条裙子需要两码蓝布。
senses.why: The measuring sense probably began with a stick of fixed length kept in a yard, and the tool gave its name to the length.
senses.whyCN: 量长度的义项大概起源于院子里一根定长的木棍，工具的名字后来变成了长度的名字。

senses.title: The railway storage area
senses.definition: the part of a railway station where trains are stored, sorted, and made ready
senses.definitionCN: 火车站中存放、编组和准备列车的那片场地
senses.example: A long line of coal cars stood idle in the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 长列煤车停在调车场里闲着。
senses.why: This is only a special case of the working ground, narrowed to the railway, where the ground is filled with rails instead of goods.
senses.whyCN: 这只是工作场地那个义项的专化，范围缩到铁路，不过地上铺满的是铁轨而不是货物。

senses.title: The home ground of an animal
senses.definition: an enclosed area where animals such as deer or poultry are kept
senses.definitionCN: 圈养鹿、家禽等动物的围起来的场地
senses.example: The deer browsed quietly in the fenced yard at the back.
senses.exampleCN: 鹿在后边围起的场院里安静地吃草。
senses.why: An enclosure for animals is the same fenced patch moved outdoors, so the word widens from people to livestock.
senses.whyCN: 圈养动物的围地就是同一块围地在户外延伸，于是这个词从人扩展到了牲畜。

intro.en: Yard is an old Germanic word for an enclosed space, related to Dutch gaard and German Garten, all from a root meaning something fenced in.
intro.cn: yard 是古老的日耳曼语词，指围起来的空间，与荷兰语 gaard、德语 Garten 同源，都出自「被围住的东西」这个词根。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic form meant a fenced enclosure, whether for people, animals, or plants.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语形式意为围起来的圈地，可以围人、围畜或围植物。

items.en: geard named an enclosed plot of ground, and the word appears in place names across England.
items.cn: 古英语 geard 指围起来的一块地，这个词出现在英格兰各地地名中。

items.en: The form settled as yard, still with the sense of an enclosed piece of ground.
items.cn: 形式固定为 yard，仍保持「围起来的一块地」的意思。

items.en: The word spread over any working ground, and the fixed stick in a yard gave Britain its measure of length.
items.cn: 这个词扩用到各种工作场地，而院子里那根定长木棍给了英国一个长度单位。

items.en: Compounds such as shipyard, farmyard, and brickyard keep the old enclosure sense alive.
items.cn: shipyard、farmyard、brickyard 这类复合词让古老的围地之义延续下来。

note.en: These words share the idea of ground, or are close in spelling to yard.
note.cn: 这些词要么与「地面、场地」的概念有关，要么在拼写上接近 yard。

entries.definition: a stick marked with units, used for measuring or for judging standards
entries.definitionCN: 同根复合词，码尺，也比喻衡量的标准

entries.definition: the area of ground around farm buildings
entries.definitionCN: 同根复合词，农家的场院

entries.definition: a piece of land where fruit trees are grown
entries.definitionCN: 同属「圈起来的园地」一类，果园

entries.definition: an enclosed area next to a building, or a place where a ball game is played
entries.definitionCN: 近义，建筑旁的封闭空地，也指球场

entries.definition: a piece of ground where flowers or vegetables are grown
entries.definitionCN: 近义，种花种菜的园地

entries.definition: an enclosed area with buildings inside it
entries.definitionCN: 近义，内有建筑的围起来的院落

normalIntro.en: The old word named a fenced patch of ground, and almost every later sense stays inside that fence.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的老义是围起来的一块地，后来几乎所有的义项都没离开那道篱笆。

normal.en: Yard goes back to a Germanic word for an enclosure, so the fence is part of the meaning.
normal.cn: yard 源自日耳曼语中「围地」的说法，所以篱笆本身就是词义的一部分。

normal.en: Add a word in front and you get a new kind of ground: farmyard, shipyard, brickyard.
normal.cn: 前面加一个词就得到一种新的场地：farmyard、shipyard、brickyard。

normal.en: Yardstick is both a measuring rod and a standard for judging, so the ground word turned into a measure of judgement.
normal.cn: yardstick 既是量尺也是判断的标准，于是一个地面词变成了评判的尺度。

normal.en: The unit of length is written yard, but it came from the same fenced plot, where a measuring stick was kept.
normal.cn: 长度单位写作 yard，但它出自同一块围地，那里放着量长度的木棍。

normal.en: In British English, yard is still the everyday word for a small back garden.
normal.cn: 在英式英语里，yard 仍是小后院的日常说法。

abstract.en: Picture a low fence behind a house; everything inside the fence is the yard, whatever you put there.
abstract.cn: 想象屋后一圈矮篱笆，篱笆里的一切都叫 yard，里面放什么都行。

abstract.en: Picture a railway ground packed with tracks: a yard is simply the house yard scaled up to the size of trains.
abstract.cn: 想象铺满铁轨的场地：yard 就是把家宅的院子放大到火车那么大。

abstract.en: Picture a stick leaning by the gate with notches cut in it; that stick is the reason a length is also called a yard.
abstract.cn: 想象门边倚着一根刻了格子的木棍；正因为这根棍，一段长度也叫 yard。

examples.en: My father keeps his old bicycle in the yard behind the house.
examples.cn: 父亲把旧自行车放在屋后的院子里。

examples.en: Trucks waited in line outside the railway yard all night.
examples.cn: 卡车在铁路调车场外排了一整夜。

examples.en: The dress needs two yards of blue cloth.
examples.cn: 这条裙子需要两码蓝布。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「丫的」——屋后圈着一块空地，孩子在里面跑得满身泥，大人喊一声「丫的，别踩水」，这块院子就是 yard。

root: 日耳曼语词根意为「围起来的一块地」，古英语作 geard，与 garden 同出一源；长度单位 yard 一般认为来自院中固定长度的量尺。

sensesIntro.en: From the fenced home ground, the word widens to working grounds of every kind and narrows to one fixed measure of length.
sensesIntro.cn: 从家宅旁围起的地出发，这个词一方面扩到各类工作场地，另一方面收拢成一个固定的长度单位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fenced patch of ground beside a building
core.cn: 核心意象：建筑旁边一块被篱笆围起的地

branches.en: The enclosed ground at home stays the everyday sense of the word.
branches.cn: 家宅旁那块围起来的地，是这个词最日常的义项。

branches.en: The same ground given over to work becomes a shipyard or a railway yard.
branches.cn: 同一块地改作干活用，就成了造船场或铁路调车场。

branches.en: A measuring stick kept in the yard gave its length the name yard.
branches.cn: 院子里放着的量尺，把它的长度命名为 yard。

branches.en: Fencing animals in turns the ground into a pen for livestock.
branches.cn: 把动物圈进去，同一块地就变成了牲畜围场。

branches.en: Whatever is fenced and set aside for use shares one image: ground under control.
branches.cn: 凡是圈起来派上用场的地都共享一个意象：被掌控的地。

intro.en: Yard is a free Germanic word that joins with nouns to name particular grounds.
intro.cn: yard 是可以独立使用的日耳曼语词，常与其他名词组合，指特定的场地。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin ancestor, so the related forms below are Old French and Germanic relatives rather than Latin roots.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源，下面的相关形式是古法语和日耳曼语亲属词，而不是拉丁词根。

items.meaning: a place where bricks are made or stored
items.example: The brickyard stood at the edge of the village.

items.meaning: ground where trains are sorted and stored

items.meaning: a paved yard enclosed by walls
items.example: A fountain stood in the middle of the courtyard.
items.exampleCN: 庭院中央立着一座喷泉。

items.example: The bell rang, and the schoolyard emptied.
items.exampleCN: 铃响了，学校操场一下空了。

definition_zh: 得到；收到；变得；到达；理解；说服
definition_en: to obtain, receive, become, reach, or cause something to happen
core_image: 伸手一抓，东西从别处落到自己手里
scene: 信箱盖啪嗒一声合上。 Did you get my letter from last Friday?
sceneCN: 这里 get 是「收到」（第 2 个义项：接收某人送来的东西）；句意为你收到我上周五的信了吗？

collocations.zh: 把事情办好；让人做某事

derivatives.zh: get + away 复合名词，义为「逃走；（度假）去处」
get 加 -er 构成，义为「获取者」

senses.title: To obtain or come to have
senses.definition: to come to have or hold something, by effort or chance
senses.definitionCN: 通过努力或机缘拥有某物
senses.example: She got a new bike for her birthday.
senses.exampleCN: 她生日得到了一辆新自行车。
senses.why: The core image is a hand closing on something, so possession is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 核心画面是手抓握东西，因此「拥有」是第一义项。

senses.title: To receive something sent or given
senses.definition: to have something delivered, sent, or offered to you
senses.definitionCN: 接收别人送达、寄来或给予的东西
senses.example: I get about twenty emails a day.
senses.exampleCN: 我每天收到大约二十封邮件。
senses.why: What arrives in your hand you have got, so reception merges with possession.
senses.whyCN: 落到手里的东西即是「得到」，接收与拥有合并。

senses.title: To become, or cause to become
senses.definition: to change state, or to make something change state
senses.definitionCN: 状态发生变化，或使某物变化
senses.example: The room gets dark very early in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 冬天的房间黑得很早。
senses.why: A change arrives at a new state the way goods arrive in hand, so becoming reuses the arrival image.
senses.whyCN: 状态变化如同货物到手，于是「变得」复用「抵达」的画面。

senses.title: To arrive at a place
senses.definition: to reach a place or destination
senses.definitionCN: 抵达某地或目的地
senses.example: We got to the station just in time.
senses.exampleCN: 我们正好及时赶到车站。
senses.why: Movement ends in the hand of the destination, so reaching a place is arrival in the same frame.
senses.whyCN: 运动终结于目的地的「手心」，到达与到手共用同一框架。

senses.title: To understand
senses.definition: to understand something said or done
senses.definitionCN: 理解所说或所做之事
senses.example: I do not get the joke, explain it again.
senses.exampleCN: 我没听懂这个笑话，再讲一遍。
senses.why: Ideas travel to the mind like objects to the hand, so catching a meaning is getting it.
senses.whyCN: 想法像物体一样落入头脑，接住意思便是「得到」意思。

senses.title: To cause or persuade
senses.definition: to make someone do something or make something happen
senses.definitionCN: 使某人做某事或使某事发生
senses.example: She got her brother to fix the radio.
senses.exampleCN: 她说服哥哥修好了收音机。
senses.why: Causing moves a thing into a new state by force of will, the causative arm of the change sense.
senses.whyCN: 使役靠意志把事物推进新状态，是「变化」义的使役分支。

intro.en: Get is a native Norse-influenced verb whose Old English and Old Norse parents merged early.
intro.cn: get 是受诺斯语影响的本土动词，古英语与古诺斯语的双亲早期融合。

items.en: Old Norse geta meant to obtain, beget, and guess.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 geta 意为获得、生育、猜中。

items.en: Old English gietan meant to obtain or beget, closely parallel.
items.cn: 古英语 gietan 意为获得、生育，与之高度平行。

items.en: Middle English merged the two into one very common verb.
items.cn: 中古英语把二者融合为一个极为常用的动词。

items.en: The past participle split into got and American gotten.
items.cn: 过去分词分化为 got 与美式 gotten。

items.en: Modern English multiplied get into hundreds of phrasal verbs.
items.cn: 现代英语把 get 繁衍出数百个短语动词。

note.en: Get, got, and gotten stack three layers, and take or receive stand beside it.
note.cn: get、got、gotten 叠成三层，take 与 receive 在旁分职。

entries.definitionCN: 美式过去分词；与 got 分工

normalIntro.en: Five grounded hooks for get.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实用法的 get 记忆钩子。

normal.en: Get is the shortest everyday verb for hand closing on things.
normal.cn: get 是「手抓住东西」的最短日常动词。

normal.en: Got covers both past tense and British past participle.
normal.cn: got 兼任过去式与英式过去分词。

normal.en: Gotten survives mainly in American speech.
normal.cn: gotten 主要存活在美式口语中。

normal.en: Get up, get on, get off, get in: position phrases everywhere.
normal.cn: get up、get on、get off、get in：位置短语无处不在。

normal.en: Get something done means arranging for it to be done.
normal.cn: get something done 表示安排把事情办成。

abstract.en: A palm opens, closes, and something new sits in it.
abstract.cn: 掌心张开、合拢，新东西落入手中。

abstract.en: The road bends and the station appears: getting there.
abstract.cn: 道路拐弯、车站出现：get 到达。

abstract.en: A lightbulb over the head is the moment you get the idea.
abstract.cn: 头顶亮起灯泡，正是 get 到主意的瞬间。

examples.en: I got your message this morning.
examples.cn: 我今天早上收到了你的消息。

examples.en: It gets cold here after October.
examples.cn: 十月之后这里开始变冷。

examples.en: She got the window repaired before winter.
examples.cn: 入冬前她找人把窗户修好了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「盖特」——伸手一盖就特快到手。

sensesIntro.en: The closed hand is the root; reception, becoming, arriving, understanding, and causing branch from it.
sensesIntro.cn: 合拢的手是根；接收、变化、到达、理解与使役都由它分支。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closing on what arrives
core.cn: 核心意象：合拢的手抓住到达之物

catching the meaning

intro.en: Get is a phrasal-verb factory, pairing with dozens of small adverbs.
intro.cn: get 是短语动词工厂，与数十个小副词搭配。

latinIntro.en: There are no Latin relatives: get is a Germanic and Norse verb.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁同源词：get 属日耳曼与诺斯语动词。

items.example: I get up at six on schooldays.
They get on well with the neighbours.
Get off at the third stop.
She got in late last night.
The cabin is their weekend getaway.
items.exampleCN: 小木屋是他们周末的避世处。

items.example: A go-getter never waits for luck.
He has gotten used to the noise.
Old texts say pride begets ruin.

definition_zh: 离开；留下；把……留给；请假；许可
definition_en: to go away from a place; to let something stay or remain; to cause something to stay behind; permission to be absent
core_image: 转身走出门口，身后留下的东西还在原处
scene: 最后一班地铁进站，他收起行李往闸机走去。 Please leave your umbrella outside the room.
sceneCN: 这里 leave 是「使某物留在某处」（第 3 个义项：留下某物）；句意为请把伞留在门外。

derivatives.zh: leave 加副词化后缀构成复合词，指「剩饭剩菜；剩余物」
来自同族词 depart（de- + partir），指「离开；出发」
leave 加施事后缀 -er，指「离开者；离职者」

senses.title: To go away from a place
senses.definition: to depart from a place or person
senses.definitionCN: 离开某地或某人
senses.example: The train leaves at eight.
senses.exampleCN: 火车八点开出。
senses.why: Going away is the picture of turning your back and moving out of range.
senses.whyCN: 「离开」就是转过身、走出范围的那幅画面。

senses.title: To let something stay
senses.definition: to allow something to remain where it is
senses.definitionCN: 允许某物留在原处
senses.example: Leave the door open, please.
senses.exampleCN: 请让门开着。
senses.why: What you do not carry away stays behind, so not-taking is a kind of leaving.
senses.whyCN: 你没带走的东西就留在原地，所以「不带走」也是一种 leave。

senses.title: To put something somewhere deliberately
senses.definition: to place something so that it stays there for someone or some purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某人或某目的把某物放在那里
senses.example: I left a note on your desk.
senses.exampleCN: 我在你桌上留了张字条。
senses.why: Placing is leaving with intent: the thing is meant to wait where it is.
senses.whyCN: 放置是带意图的留下：那东西就是要在原地等着。

senses.title: To cause a state or result
senses.definition: to make something be in a particular state after an action
senses.definitionCN: 使某物在动作之后处于特定状态
senses.example: The storm left the streets covered in leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后街道上盖满落叶。
senses.why: The actor walks away but the effect stays, so the result is what he left.
senses.whyCN: 施动者走了，效果却留下，所以结果就是他留下的东西。

senses.title: To give by will or transfer
senses.definition: to give property or responsibility to someone after death or on departure
senses.definitionCN: 死后或离开时把财产或责任交给某人
senses.example: She left the house to her daughter.
senses.exampleCN: 她把房子留给女儿。
senses.why: Departure from life or a job passes things to those who stay.
senses.whyCN: 从生命或职位离开时，东西就传给留下的人。

senses.title: Permission; time off
senses.definition: official permission to be absent, or the period of absence itself
senses.definitionCN: 获准缺席的正式许可，或缺席的那段时间
senses.example: He is on sick leave this week.
senses.exampleCN: 他本周休病假。
senses.why: Being away needs approval, so the word names both the permission and the absence itself.
senses.whyCN: 离开需要批准，所以这个词既指许可也指缺席期本身。

senses.title: To stop doing something
senses.definition: to stop doing or dealing with something
senses.definitionCN: 停止做或不再处理某事
senses.example: Leave the arguing and start the work.
senses.exampleCN: 别吵了，开始干活吧。
senses.why: Walking away from an activity is leaving it behind like a place.
senses.whyCN: 从一件事上抽身，就像离开一个地方。

senses.title: To depend on someone else
senses.definition: to let another person decide or handle something
senses.definitionCN: 让别人决定或处理某事
senses.example: Leave it to me.
senses.exampleCN: 交给我吧。
senses.why: You walk away from the decision and it waits in the hands of whoever stays.
senses.whyCN: 你从决定旁边走开，它就留在留下的人手里。

intro.en: Leave comes from Old English laefan "to allow, leave behind", from Germanic laibjan, related to a root meaning "to remain".
intro.cn: leave 来自古英语 laefan「准许、留下」，出自日耳曼语 laibjan，与意为「留存」的词根相关。

items.en: Old English laefan meant 'to leave, allow, bequeath', already covering both going away and letting stay.
items.cn: 古英语 laefan 意为「离开、准许、遗赠」，已同时涵盖离去与留存两方向。

items.en: Germanic laibjan is behind the English verb and related to German bleiben 'to remain', from a root meaning 'to stick, stay'.
items.cn: 日耳曼语 laibjan 是英语动词的来源，并与德语 bleiben「停留」同源，词根意为「粘住、留下」。

items.en: Norse influence may have strengthened the sense of permission and departure in northern English.
items.cn: 北欧语的影响可能强化了英格兰北部用法中「许可」与「离去」的义项。

items.en: In Middle English leave developed the noun sense of permission, then of authorized absence.
items.cn: 中古英语里 leave 发展出「许可」的名词义，进而指获批的缺席。

items.en: Modern English kept both directions: go away, let stay, and added the workplace holiday sense.
items.cn: 现代英语保留双向用法：离去、任其留下，并新增了职场休假义。

note.en: Group one flags words that only look alike; group two collects words of going away and staying.
note.cn: 第一组标出仅外形相近的词；第二组收集「离去」与「留存」的词。

entries.definition: The plant word; ends in -f not -ve and belongs to Germanic laub.
entries.definitionCN: 植物词；词尾是 -f 不是 -ve，属于日耳曼语 laub 词族。

entries.definition: From Old English libban "to live"; only the letters after l-i look close.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古英语 libban「活着」；只是 l-i 之后的字母相像。

entries.definition: Someone who leaves, as in school leavers.
entries.definitionCN: 离开的人，如 school leaver（离校生）。

entries.definition: What is left over after the rest is gone.
entries.definitionCN: 其余部分走后剩下的东西。

entries.definition: To go away, especially on a journey; leave is the everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 离去，尤指启程；leave 是日常用词。

entries.definition: To stop or resign; it stresses ending an activity or job.
entries.definitionCN: 停止或辞职；强调终结某项活动或工作。

entries.definition: To leave something completely and finally, often without care.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底且最终地抛下，常含不顾不管。

entries.definition: To stay where you are; the staying side of the same picture.
entries.definitionCN: 留在原地；同一画面的「留下」一侧。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real family and fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实词族与固定搭配。

normal.en: Old English laefan meant 'leave behind, allow', so both directions are ancient.
normal.cn: 古英语 laefan 意为「留下、准许」，两个方向都很古老。

normal.en: German bleiben "to remain" is a cousin from the same root.
normal.cn: 德语 bleiben「停留」是同一词根的表亲。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: leave for, leave behind, leave out, take French leave.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：动身前往、留下、遗漏、不告而别。

normal.en: The past form left also works as an adjective, as in the left side.
normal.cn: 过去式 left 还能作形容词，如「左边」。

normal.en: On leave means officially away: sick leave, annual leave, maternity leave.
normal.cn: on leave 指获批离岗：病假、年假、产假。

abstract.en: Picture your footprints behind you on wet sand as you walk off.
abstract.cn: 想象你走开后，湿沙上留下一串脚印。

abstract.en: Picture a note under a magnet on the fridge, waiting for someone.
abstract.cn: 想象冰箱磁铁下压着一张字条，等人来取。

abstract.en: Picture a will passing keys to the one who stays.
abstract.cn: 想象一纸遗嘱把钥匙交给留下的人。

examples.en: We leave for Shanghai early tomorrow morning.
examples.cn: 我们明早动身去上海。

examples.en: The night shift left the tools exactly where they found them.
examples.cn: 夜班把工具原样留在原地。

examples.en: She took two weeks of leave after the project ended.
examples.cn: 项目结束后她休了两周假。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离吾」——离吾而去 → 离开；留下

root: 古英语 laefan「留下、准许」，出自日耳曼语 laibjan，与「留存」义词根相关；与德语 bleiben 同源是学界共识。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split along two arrows: going away yourself, or letting things stay behind when you go.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿两支箭头展开：自己走开，或走开时让东西留在后面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a doorway; you step through and things stay on the far side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道门；你跨过去，东西留在另一边。

branches.en: WALKING OFF: from places and from activities alike.
branches.cn: 走开：既离开地方，也抽离活动。

branches.en: THINGS THAT WAIT: letting stay, or placing on purpose.
branches.cn: 等待之物：任其留下，或有意放置。

branches.en: THE AFTER-EFFECT: results left hanging in the air.
branches.cn: 后续效果：留在空气里的结果。

branches.en: PASSING ON: property and duties go to those who stay.
branches.cn: 传递：财产与职责交给留下的人。

branches.en: OFFICIAL AWAY: permission, holiday, and handing decisions to others.
branches.cn: 获批离场：许可、假期，以及把决定交给别人。

intro.en: Leave is a native Germanic verb with no Latin prefix; its family is small and built with native suffixes.
intro.cn: leave 是日耳曼本族动词，没有拉丁前缀；词族不大，用本族后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: No established Latin cognate exists, so the Latin section stays empty; the items show native word-building.
latinIntro.cn: 没有确证的拉丁同族词，拉丁部分留空；条目展示本族构词。

它把 leave 变成 leaver。
它与 leave 合成 leftover。
冰箱里塞满冷掉的剩菜。

items.example: Three apples were left on the plate.

items.exampleCN: 德语 bleiben 保留了形式。

definition_en: the use of scientific knowledge for practical purposes, or the machines it produces
core_image: 实验室里成排的机器与屏幕同时亮起
scene: 新技术让偏远村庄也用上了网络。 New technology brought the internet to remote villages.
sceneCN: 这里 technology 是「科技、技术」（第 1 个义项）；句意：新技术让偏远村庄也用上了网络。

derivatives.zh: 技术的；科技的

senses.title: Applied scientific knowledge
senses.definition: the use of scientific knowledge to solve practical problems
senses.definitionCN: 把科学知识用于解决实际问题
senses.example: New technology brought the internet to remote villages.
senses.exampleCN: 新技术让偏远村庄也用上了网络。
senses.why: The Greek compound means the systematic study of a craft.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊语复合词意为对一门技艺的系统论述。

senses.title: The machines and systems produced
senses.definition: the machines, systems, and tools that such knowledge creates
senses.definitionCN: 由这类知识造出的机器、系统与工具
senses.example: The hospital invested in new medical technology.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院投资购买了新的医疗设备。
senses.why: The knowledge and the objects it builds share one name.
senses.whyCN: 知识与它造出的物件共用同一个名字。

intro.en: Technology began as the study of a craft, not as machines.
intro.cn: technology 最初指对技艺的研究，而非机器。

items.en: Techne meant craft, and logia meant study.
items.cn: techne 意为技艺，logia 意为论述、研究。

items.en: Tekhnologia meant a systematic treatment of an art.
items.cn: tekhnologia 意为对一门技艺的系统论述。

items.en: Technology entered English as the study of arts.
items.cn: technology 最初进入英语时指技艺之学。

items.en: It shifted to applied science and industry.
items.cn: 它转向应用科学与工业。

items.en: It now also names the machines themselves.
items.cn: 如今它也指机器本身。

note.en: Technology is compared with look-alike forms and with words for tools and science.
note.cn: 把 technology 与形近形式以及表示工具与科学的词作对比。

definition_zh: 第十四；第十四个（的）；十四分之一
definition_en: coming after the thirteenth in order; one part of fourteen equal parts
core_image: 赛道上第十四个标记：排在这条队伍的倒数靠后位置
scene: 运动会上，小林排在第十四位出发，前面还有十三名选手。 Xiao Lin started fourteenth in the race.
sceneCN: 这里 fourteenth 是「第十四（位）」的意思（第 1 个义项：排序中的第十四）；他在十四名选手里列第十四个出发。

derivatives.zh: fourteenth 的基数词，义为「十四」
数列相邻序数词，义为「第四」
数列相邻序数词，义为「第十五」

senses.title: Coming after thirteen in order
senses.definition: the position after the thirteenth item in a series
senses.definitionCN: 序列中排在第十三之后的那个位置。
senses.example: This is the fourteenth time she has visited the museum.
senses.exampleCN: 这是她第十四次参观这家博物馆。
senses.why: The -th suffix turns the number four into an order marker.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -th 把数字变成次序标记。

senses.title: One part of fourteen equal parts
senses.definition: one of fourteen equal parts of a whole
senses.definitionCN: 整体被分成十四等份中的一份。
senses.example: Each runner got a fourteenth of the prize money.
senses.exampleCN: 每名选手分到奖金的十四分之一。
senses.why: Ordinals also measure fractions of a whole.
senses.whyCN: 序数词也可以量分数。

intro.en: Fourteenth is fourteen plus the Old English order suffix -tha.
intro.cn: fourteenth 是 fourteen 加上古英语次序后缀 -tha。

items.en: Feowerteogotha marked the fourteenth position in Old English counting.
items.cn: 古英语 feowerteogotha 标记「第十四」的位次。

items.en: The suffix -tha was the standard order maker, surviving as modern -th.
items.cn: 后缀 -tha 是标准造序词成分，延续为现代 -th。

items.en: The form fourtenthe appeared in dated records and lists.
items.cn: 中古英语形式 fourtenthe 见于记日与列表文献。

items.en: The spelling settled as fourteenth, matching fourteen.
items.cn: 拼写定型为 fourteenth，与 fourteen 对应。

items.en: Fraction use and century references like the fourteenth century became common.
items.cn: 分数用法与 the fourteenth century 等世纪表达普及。

note.en: Words shaped like fourteenth and its ordinal neighbours.
note.cn: 与 fourteenth 形近的词及序数词邻居。

entries.definition: the ordinal of forty; easy to confuse with fourteenth
entries.definitionCN: 第四十；forty 的序数词，与 fourteenth 易混。

entries.definition: the cardinal that fourteenth builds on
entries.definitionCN: 十四；fourteenth 的基数。

entries.definition: the next ordinal in the series
entries.definitionCN: 第十五；序数链的下一环。

entries.definition: coming at the end of a series
entries.definitionCN: 最后的；序位表达的高端。

entries.definition: second from the last
entries.definitionCN: 倒数第二；比 fourteenth 更抽象的位次词。

entries.definition: used to introduce the fourteenth point in a formal list
entries.definitionCN: 第十四（正式列举用语）；fourteenth 加 -ly 的书面连接词。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on the -th order marker and date uses of fourteenth.
normalIntro.cn: 围绕 -th 序数标记与日期用法的五条记忆钩子。

normal.en: Add -th to fourteen to make the order word fourteenth.
normal.cn: fourteen 加 -th 变成序数词 fourteenth。

normal.en: Say dates aloud: the fourteenth of March.
normal.cn: 朗读日期练习：the fourteenth of March。

normal.en: In history class, remember the fourteenth century as the 1300s.
normal.cn: 历史课上把 the fourteenth century 记作十四世纪（一三〇〇年代）。

normal.en: Chain the ordinals: fourth, fourteenth, fortieth.
normal.cn: 串序数链：fourth、fourteenth、fortieth。

normal.en: A fourteenth of something is one slice of fourteen slices.
normal.cn: a fourteenth 就是十四等份中的一份。

abstract.en: Picture fourteen runners, the last-but-one wearing number fourteen.
abstract.cn: 想象十四名选手中戴着十四号号码布的 runners。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar square circled in red pen.
abstract.cn: 想象日历上被红笔圈住的方格。

abstract.en: Picture a cake cut into fourteen thin slices.
abstract.cn: 想象被切成十四薄片的蛋糕。

examples.en: Valentine's Day falls on the fourteenth of February.
examples.cn: 情人节在二月十四日。

examples.en: The fourteenth century saw the building of many town walls.
examples.cn: 十四世纪修建了许多城墙。

examples.en: He finished fourteenth in his first marathon.
examples.cn: 他的首场马拉松跑了第十四名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛提恩斯」——十四（fourteen）后面再咬一口「丝」（-th 的尾音），丝是「次序之线」：fourteenth 就是第十四。

root: fourteenth 出自古英语 feowerteogotha：fourteen（十四）+ -tha（次序后缀，今作 -th）。属本土序数词构造，无拉丁成分；兼作分数「十四分之一」。

sensesIntro.en: Fourteenth marks order in lists, dates, and centuries, plus the fraction one of fourteen.
sensesIntro.cn: fourteenth 标记列表、日期、世纪中的位次，兼表十四分之一。

core.cn: 核心意象：插在队伍第十四位的标记

branches.en: The position after the thirteenth
branches.cn: 排在第十三之后的位次

branches.cn: 同一个后缀同时管排名与切分

intro.cn: fourteenth 展示了日耳曼序数后缀 -th 在数词上的运作。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the suffix family is entirely native.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁词根；后缀家族完全是本土的。

definition_zh: 塔；高楼；塔楼；（作动词）高耸；远远高出
definition_en: a tall narrow structure or building that stands far above what is around it
core_image: 一座瘦高的石塔，从周围的屋顶里直插上去
scene: 黄昏的旧城，屋顶一片低矮，只有教堂的石砌高塔越过了所有屋脊。 The clock tower can be seen from the harbour on a clear evening.
sceneCN: 这里 tower 是「塔」（第 1 个义项：高而窄的建筑物）；句意为天气晴好的傍晚从港湾就能望见那座钟塔。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「高耸的；极其高大的」
由过去分词转化，义为「有塔楼的」
来自同一拉丁词源的小词，义为「小塔；角楼」

senses.title: A tall narrow structure
senses.definition: a building or structure much taller than it is wide, often used for watching, bells, or water
senses.definitionCN: 高度远大于宽度的建筑或结构，常用于瞭望、敲钟或储水
senses.example: The tower has stood on the hill for six hundred years.
senses.exampleCN: 这座塔已在山上矗立了六百年。
senses.why: The Latin source names a tower, and this is the plain architectural sense still at the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源本身就是「塔」，这是这个词至今居中心位置的建筑本义。

senses.title: A high building of many floors
senses.definition: a tall building with many storeys, especially one for offices or flats
senses.definitionCN: 层数很多的建筑，尤指办公楼或住宅
senses.example: They work on the twentieth floor of that tower.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在那座高楼的二十层上班。
senses.why: When cities grew upward, the tall vertical shape of the stone tower was simply reused for new buildings.
senses.whyCN: 当城市向上生长时，石塔那种高而直的形态就被直接套用到新建筑上。

senses.title: To rise far above the surroundings
senses.definition: used of something that stands much taller than the things near it
senses.definitionCN: 指某物比周围的东西高得多
senses.example: The old tree towers over the garden wall.
senses.exampleCN: 那棵老树高过花园的围墙。
senses.why: A building so vertical becomes a gesture, and the noun turns into a verb for standing tall.
senses.whyCN: 建筑如此竖直就变成了一种姿态，名词便转为「站得高」的动词。

senses.title: To be far greater in another quality
senses.definition: to be far greater than someone or something in ability, size, or importance
senses.definitionCN: 在能力、规模或重要性上远远超过某人或某物
senses.example: In debate she towers over her opponents.
senses.exampleCN: 在辩论中她远远胜过对手。
senses.why: Height is the easiest metaphor for excellence, so towering over rivals means being much greater.
senses.whyCN: 「高」是形容卓越最容易的比喻，所以高于对手就是远胜对手。

senses.title: A place of proud distance
senses.definition: in phrases like ivory tower, a protected place far from ordinary life
senses.definitionCN: 如 ivory tower 一类说法中，指远离日常生活的保护区
senses.example: Critics say the scholars have retired to an ivory tower.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者说这些学者退进了象牙塔。
senses.why: A tower keeps its people above the street and away from it, so the image comes to mean proud isolation.
senses.whyCN: 塔让人位于街道之上并与之隔绝，于是这个形象转指高傲的自我隔离。

intro.en: Tower comes from Latin turris through Old French tor, and the same Latin noun gave Greek island towns such as Tower names across Europe; the more distant origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: tower 经古法语 tor 来自拉丁语 turris；更深来源不确定。同一个拉丁名词在整个欧洲派生出了众多塔名。

items.en: Greek tyrris is cited as a forerunner of the Latin word, but the link is debated.
items.cn: 一般认为希腊语 tyrris 是拉丁词的先形，但这层联系仍有争议。

items.en: Latin turris names a tall fortified structure, and it is borrowed by many languages of the empire.
items.cn: 拉丁语 turris 指高耸的防御性建筑，被帝国境内的许多语言借走。

items.en: Old French tor and tur keep the military sense and pass into the language of castles.
items.cn: 古法语 tor、tur 保留了军事含义，进入城堡用语。

items.en: Middle English tower first means a castle keep or a church bell tower.
items.cn: 中古英语 tower 最初指城堡主楼或教堂钟楼。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the word widens to office blocks and water works.
items.cn: 十九、二十世纪，这个词扩展到办公楼与供水设施。

items.en: The figurative ivory tower becomes common after French criticism of writers in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪法国人批评作家脱离现实之后，比喻性的 ivory tower 才流行起来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words easily confused in spelling with tower, and the near-meaning group gathers tall vertical things.
note.cn: 形近组收集拼写易与 tower 混淆的词，近义组收集高而竖直的事物。

entries.definitionCN: 尖顶；塔尖

entries.definitionCN: 摩天大楼

entries.definitionCN: 教堂尖塔

normalIntro.en: These memories work from the Latin stem, from the castle and water compounds, and from the verb of standing tall.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条从拉丁词干、城堡与储水的复合词，以及「高耸」的动词用法入手。

normal.en: Turris is the Latin tower, and it stands behind turret as well.
normal.cn: turris 是拉丁语的塔，turret 也由它而来。

normal.en: Clock tower, water tower, tower block: the word sits in front to say what the tall thing is for.
normal.cn: clock tower、water tower、tower block，本词放前面说明这座高物是做什么用的。

normal.en: The verb use is easy: towers over simply means stands much taller than.
normal.cn: 动词用法很简单：towers over 就是「比……高得多地立着」。

normal.en: Ivory tower is a set phrase and its meaning is isolation, not height.
normal.cn: ivory tower 是固定说法，重点在隔离，不在高度。

normal.en: Tower and towel differ by one letter, so remember the tower has an r for rock.
normal.cn: tower 与 towel 只差一个字母，记住塔有 r，r 代表石头。

abstract.en: Picture a thin grey finger of stone poking above a whole town of roofs.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细细的灰色石指，从全城的屋顶上方伸出来。

abstract.en: Think of a shadow that is long at sunset because the thing casting it is so tall.
abstract.cn: 想日落时那道很长的影子，因为投下影子的东西太高了。

abstract.en: A tower is height that has been made permanent.
abstract.cn: 塔是被固定下来的高度。

examples.en: The water tower supplies the whole village.
examples.cn: 这座水塔为整个村子供水。

examples.en: He towers over everyone in his class.
examples.cn: 他比班上所有人都高出一截。

examples.en: The tower was struck by lightning last summer.
examples.cn: 去年夏天这座塔被雷击中了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「塔窝」——塔里有个窝，抬头看塔，越看越高。

root: 拉丁语 turris（塔）→ 古法语 tor → 中古英语 tower。同族或同源词有 turret；更早的希腊语来源一般认为相关，但尚未定论。

sensesIntro.en: From one upright stone shape the entry rises into the modern high building, then tilts into the verb of being taller, then into superiority, and finally into the tower as a place of proud isolation.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一块竖直的石头形态出发，本词长成现代高楼，再倾斜为「更高」的动词，进而表示优越，最后成为高傲隔离之所。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow vertical stone rising above everything around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座窄而竖直的石构物，高出周围一切。

branches.en: The fort or bell structure itself.
The modern high building.
The act of standing much higher.
The metaphor of superiority.
The tower as a place apart from the world.
branches.cn: 作为远离尘世之处的塔。

intro.en: The word is a simple borrowing from Latin with no productive English suffix, and its compounds are built by putting the purpose in front.
intro.cn: 本词是直接借入的拉丁词，没有能产的英语后缀，其复合词靠把用途前置来构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun turris is the source of the English word and of its diminutive cousin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁名词 turris 既是英语本词的来源，也是它的指小近亲的来源。

items.exampleCN: ivory tower 是表示隔离的说法。

definition_zh: 离开；不在；消失
definition_en: to or at a distance from a place, or not present, or until gone
core_image: 走廊上一个人转身走远
scene: 走廊上，她一句话没说就转身走开了。 She walked away without a word.
sceneCN: 这里 away 是「离开」（第 1 个义项：从原处走开）；句意为她一言不发地走开了。

derivatives.zh: 遥远的
外卖
远离

senses.title: To a distance
senses.definition: to or at a distance from a place
senses.definitionCN: 到离开某地的地方，或在远处
senses.example: She walked away without a word.
senses.exampleCN: 她一言不发地走开了。
senses.why: The old phrase meant on the way, so moving off from a place is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 古短语意为在路上，所以从某处走开就是第一义。

senses.title: Not present
senses.definition: not at home or not in the usual place
senses.definitionCN: 不在家或不在通常所在之处
senses.example: My father is away on business.
senses.exampleCN: 我父亲出差去了。
senses.why: A person who has moved off is simply not there, which gives the sense of absent.
senses.whyCN: 人走开了，就是单纯不在这里，于是有「不在」的义项。

senses.title: Until gone
senses.definition: until something has gone completely
senses.definitionCN: 直到某物完全消失或耗尽
senses.example: The snow melted away.
senses.exampleCN: 雪融化消失了。
senses.why: Moving off to the last bit leaves nothing behind, which gives the sense of gone for good.
senses.whyCN: 一直移动到一点都不剩，就什么都没留下，于是有「消失殆尽」。

intro.en: The recorded history of away is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 away 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Onweg meant on the way or from this place.
items.cn: onweg 意为在路上或离开此地。

items.en: Middle English shortened the phrase into one word.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个短语缩短为一个词。

items.en: English used away for moving off from a place.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪用 away 指从某处走开。

items.en: Later it covered being gone from home.
items.cn: 后来它也指不在家。

items.en: Today right away is a common phrase for at once.
items.cn: 今天 right away 是表示「立刻」的常用短语。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: The adjective for a distant place.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指遥远的。

entries.definition: Food taken away to eat elsewhere.
entries.definitionCN: 指带走食用的饭菜。

entries.definition: It looks close but names a road or a method.
entries.definitionCN: 外观相近，但指道路或方法。

entries.definition: It stresses leaving a surface or a place.
entries.definitionCN: 强调离开某个表面或地点。

entries.definition: It stresses being separated by a distance.
entries.definitionCN: 强调被距离分开。

entries.definition: It states plainly that someone is not here.
entries.definitionCN: 直接说明某人不在这里。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: on the way meant moving along: away marks the distance left behind.
normal.cn: on the way 意为在路上：away 标记被留在身后的距离。

normal.en: The same family also gives faraway and takeaway.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 faraway 与 takeaway。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase go away.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「走开」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of away in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 away 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: to or at a distance from a place, or not present, or until gone.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「离开」时用它。

abstract.en: Picture a person turning on a corridor and walking off.
abstract.cn: 想象走廊上一个人转身走远。

abstract.en: The same picture can be literal in one sentence and figurative in another.
abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of away grows from one core image: a person turning on a corridor and walking off.
sensesIntro.cn: away 的各个义项都从同一个核心意象生长出来：走廊上一个人转身走远。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person turning on a corridor and walking off
core.cn: 核心意象：走廊上一个人转身走远

branches.cn: 义项 01 覆盖最字面的用法：离开、到别处。

branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更宽泛的日常用法：不在、外出。

branches.en: Sense 03 covers a further use: Until gone.
branches.cn: 义项 03 覆盖更靠后的一种用法：消失、用完。

definition_zh: 微笑；笑容；微笑着表示
definition_en: a happy expression with the corners of the mouth turned up, or to make such an expression
core_image: 嘴角上扬的一张温暖笑脸
scene: 她对我露出温暖的微笑。 She gave me a warm smile.

senses.title: A happy expression
senses.definition: an expression of pleasure in which the corners of the mouth turn up
senses.definitionCN: 嘴角上扬、表示愉快的表情
senses.example: She gave me a warm smile.
senses.exampleCN: 她对我露出温暖的微笑。
senses.why: This is the noun sense of the expression.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示表情的名词义项。

senses.title: To make a smile
senses.definition: to make a happy expression with the mouth
senses.definitionCN: 用嘴做出愉快的表情
senses.example: He smiled at the good news.
senses.exampleCN: 他听到好消息笑了。

senses.title: Show by smiling

senses.example: She smiled her agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 她微笑着表示同意。
senses.why: A smile can carry a whole message.

senses.title: A deep round container for cooking or storing
senses.definition: a deep round vessel, usually with a lid, used for cooking food or keeping things in
senses.definitionCN: 通常带盖的深圆容器，用来做饭或存放东西
senses.example: She left the soup simmering in a heavy iron pot.
senses.exampleCN: 她把汤留在一口厚重的铁锅里慢慢炖着。
senses.why: Old English pott named a rounded vessel before it named any particular use, so cooking is only one of the jobs the container was given.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 pott 先指一种圆鼓鼓的容器，并不限定用途，做饭只是人们后来交给它的活儿之一。

senses.title: The amount a pot holds
senses.definition: as much as a pot contains, used as a rough measure in cooking and serving
senses.definitionCN: 一锅或一罐所装的分量，在烹饪与待客时用作粗略的计量
senses.example: He made a pot of coffee for the four of them.
senses.exampleCN: 他煮了一壶咖啡给四个人喝。
senses.why: A container word slides to its contents because the two are always seen together, and English lets pot measure coffee or soup without any extra suffix.
senses.whyCN: 容器和里面的东西总是一起出现，于是容器词顺势指内容物；英语不必加后缀，pot 就能直接量咖啡或汤。

senses.title: A container for a growing plant
senses.definition: a round container filled with soil in which a plant is grown indoors or on a windowsill
senses.definitionCN: 装满泥土、在室内或窗台上种花的圆形容器
senses.example: The basil on the windowsill needs a bigger pot.
senses.exampleCN: 窗台上的罗勒需要换一个更大的花盆。
senses.why: When clay vessels were stood in gardens and on windowsills, the same word that named a kitchen vessel came to name the vessel a plant lives in.
senses.whyCN: 当陶制容器被摆到院子里和窗台上，原本指厨房器皿的词就转而指植物所住的容器。

senses.title: To plant something in a pot
senses.definition: to put a plant into a container filled with soil so that it can grow there
senses.definitionCN: 把植物放进装了土的容器里，让它在其中生长
senses.example: She potted the young tomato plants before the first frost.
senses.exampleCN: 初霜之前，她把番茄苗移栽进了盆里。
senses.why: English turns nouns into verbs without adding anything, so the name of the container became the name of the act of putting a plant into it.
senses.whyCN: 英语可以不添任何成分就把名词用作动词，于是容器的名字变成了「把植物放进容器」这个动作的名字。

senses.title: The money staked in a card game
senses.definition: the total amount of money that players have put into the middle of the table in a game of cards
senses.definitionCN: 牌局中玩家押到桌面中央的钱的总数
senses.example: By the last hand there was a small fortune in the pot.
senses.exampleCN: 到最后一局时，桌上的赌注已经是一笔不小的钱。
senses.why: Card players drop their stakes into a central dish, and English simply moved the name of that dish onto the money it held, keeping the picture of a shared vessel.
senses.whyCN: 牌手把赌注丢进桌子中央的盘子里，英语直接把盘子的名字挪到里面的钱上，共用一只容器的画面留了下来。

intro.en: Pot is an old Germanic vessel word. Whether it was lent to Latin or borrowed from Latin is still argued, so the deeper origin is usually given with a hedge.
intro.cn: pot 是一个古老的日耳曼语容器词。它究竟是借给了拉丁语，还是从拉丁语借来，至今仍有争论，所以更远的来历通常要加一句「一般认为」。

items.en: A reconstructed Germanic word for a rounded vessel; the asterisk marks a form rebuilt by comparing later languages, not one found written down.
items.cn: 这是为「圆形容器」重构出来的日耳曼语词；星号表示它是靠比较后世语言推出来的，并非有文字记录的形式。

items.en: Old English pott names a deep vessel, and this is the form English has kept to the present day.
items.cn: 古英语 pott 指深腹容器，英语一直把这个形式保留到今天。

items.en: Many dictionaries think the Germanic word was borrowed from a Vulgar Latin pottus for a drinking vessel, but the direction of the borrowing is not settled.
items.cn: 不少词典认为这个日耳曼词借自俗拉丁语 pottus（饮器），但借用的方向至今没有定论。

items.en: If the vessel word does go back to Latin, its ultimate root is potare, to drink, with potio, a drink, beside it.
items.cn: 如果这个容器词确实可追溯到拉丁语，它更远的根就是 potare（饮），旁边的 potio 意为饮料。

items.en: Modern English extended the vessel to flower pots, to the stakes in a card game, and to the verb of planting.
items.cn: 现代英语把这件容器扩展到花盆、牌桌上的赌注，还把它用作「栽种」的动词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the vessel itself; the near-meaning group gathers other kitchen and table containers.
note.cn: 形近组收直接由这件容器构成的词；近义组收厨房与餐桌上其他容器词。

entries.definition: Pots and other objects made of baked clay.
entries.definitionCN: 陶土烧成的锅、罐等器物；陶器。

entries.definition: A person who makes pots and other clay vessels.
entries.definitionCN: 制作陶罐等器皿的人；陶工。

entries.definition: As much as a single pot will hold.
entries.definitionCN: 一锅或一罐的分量。

entries.definition: A thick soup or stew cooked in a pot.
entries.definitionCN: 在锅里熬成的浓汤；菜糊。

entries.definition: A shallow metal container used for cooking.
entries.definitionCN: 较浅的金属锅；平底锅。

entries.definition: A container with a spout and handle, used for boiling water.
entries.definitionCN: 带壶嘴和把手、用来烧水的壶。

entries.definition: A wide-mouthed container of glass or clay, used for storing food.
entries.definitionCN: 广口的玻璃或陶制容器，用来存放食物；罐子。

entries.definition: A very large pot used for boiling over a fire.
entries.definitionCN: 在火上煮东西用的大锅。

normalIntro.en: The word has named a round vessel for over a thousand years, and most of its other uses are that vessel seen from a different angle.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词指一种圆容器已有一千多年，它其余的用法大多只是从不同角度去看这件容器。

normal.en: Old English pott already meant a deep vessel, so the word is older than any recipe written in English.
normal.cn: 古英语 pott 已经是「深容器」的意思，所以这个词比任何英语写成的菜谱都老。

normal.en: Add -ful and the vessel becomes a measure: a potful is as much as it takes to fill one.
normal.cn: 加上 -ful，容器就变成量词：potful 就是装满一只锅的分量。

normal.en: Add -er and you get the person, potter, the one who makes the vessel.
normal.cn: 加上 -er 就得到人：potter 是做这件容器的人。

normal.en: Add -ery and you get the craft and its place: pottery is both the ware and the workshop.
normal.cn: 加上 -ery 就得到手艺与场所：pottery 既指陶器，也指陶艺作坊。

normal.en: Pot luck and go to pot keep the old household picture: whatever the pot happens to hold, or a house gone to ruin.
normal.cn: pot luck 与 go to pot 都留着旧日居家的画面：锅里碰巧有什么，或者一个家败落下去。

abstract.en: A pot is defined by what it can hold, so the word slides easily from vessel to contents to the money on a table.
abstract.cn: 锅由它能装什么来定义，所以这个词很自然地从事物滑到内容，再滑到桌上的钱。

abstract.en: Round, deep and lidded: the shape is the meaning, and every new use keeps that shape somewhere in view.
abstract.cn: 圆、深、有盖：形状本身就是词义，每个新用法都在某处保留着这个形状。

abstract.en: The same word feeds a kitchen, a garden and a card table, because all three need something to put things into.
abstract.cn: 同一个词同时养活厨房、花园和牌桌，因为这三处都需要一个能装东西的容器。

examples.en: She left the soup simmering in a heavy iron pot.
examples.cn: 她把汤留在一口厚重的铁锅里慢慢炖着。

examples.en: He potted the seedlings on the balcony.
examples.cn: 他在阳台上把幼苗栽进了盆里。

examples.en: There was enough money in the pot to pay for the trip.
examples.cn: 桌上的赌注足够支付这趟旅行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泡特」——汤在锅里泡得特别久；pot 就是锅、罐，也能当动词表示栽进盆里。

root: 中古英语 pott 上承古英语 pott；一般认为与俗拉丁语 pottus（饮器）有关，更远的根或为拉丁语 potare（饮），但借用方向仍有争议。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a round vessel; the senses then follow what the vessel holds, where it stands, and what people do with it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一件圆容器；义项随后沿着它装什么、摆在哪里、人们拿它做什么展开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick pot on a stove, its lid lifted again and again by steam.
core.cn: 核心意象：灶上一口厚底锅，锅盖被蒸汽一次次顶起。

branches.en: a heavy pot breathing steam on a low flame
branches.cn: 小火上冒着蒸汽的厚锅

branches.en: a pot of coffee shared by four cups
branches.cn: 一壶分给四只杯子的咖啡

branches.en: a windowsill herb waiting for more soil
branches.cn: 窗台上等着换土的那盆香草

branches.en: fingers pressing soil around a young root
branches.cn: 手指把土按在幼苗根旁

branches.en: coins and notes piled in the middle of a table

intro.en: One old Germanic noun, pott, supplies the stem; English then builds a measure with -ful, a person with -er, a craft with -ery, and a participle with -ed.
intro.cn: 一个古老的日耳曼名词 pott 提供词干，英语再用 -ful 造量、用 -er 造人、用 -ery 造手艺、用 -ed 造分词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

pots and the craft of making them
planted or preserved in a pot
the act of planting in a pot

definition_zh: 活泼的；充满活力的；生动的；热闹的；鲜艳的；热烈的
definition_en: full of energy and enthusiasm, vivid and full of interest, busy with activity, bright in colour, or vigorous in argument
core_image: 一群孩子在院子里追着皮球跑，笑声把安静的午后掀了起来
scene: 午后的院子里，几个孩子追着皮球跑，笑声一阵接一阵。 The lively children kept the whole street awake with their shouting.
sceneCN: 这里 lively 是「活泼的」（第 1 个义项：精力充沛、爱动）；句意为这些活泼的孩子用喊声让整条街都醒着。图中可辨识物件：院子、皮球、奔跑的孩子。

pos.zh: 活泼的；生动的；热闹的；鲜艳的；热烈的

derivatives.zh: 由 lively 加 -ness 构成，义为「活泼；生动」
与 lively 同源，义为「生命；生活」
与 lively 同源，义为「活着；居住」

senses.title: Full of energy and enthusiasm
senses.definition: full of energy, movement and enthusiasm, especially in the way a person or animal behaves
senses.definitionCN: 充满精力、动作与热情，尤指人或动物的举止
senses.example: The lively children kept the whole street awake with their shouting.
senses.exampleCN: 这些活泼的孩子用喊声让整条街都醒着。
senses.why: Old English liflic joins lif, life, to -lic, the suffix of likeness; the first sense is a creature visibly full of life, moving and making sound.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 liflic 把 lif（生命）与表示「像……一样」的后缀 -lic 连在一起；最早的义项就是看得见生命在动的活物，会跑会叫。

senses.title: Vivid and full of interest
senses.definition: vivid, interesting and full of imaginative detail, as in a lively description or a lively imagination
senses.definitionCN: 生动有趣、充满想象细节，如生动的描写或丰富的想象力
senses.example: She gave a lively account of the market on a rainy morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她把雨中清晨的集市讲得活灵活现。
senses.why: A description that keeps moving in the mind is felt to have life; the energy of a body is transferred to words, so a vivid account is called lively.
senses.whyCN: 一段在脑海里不断活动的描写会被觉得有生命；身体的能量转移到了文字上，于是生动的叙述就被称作 lively。

senses.title: Busy and full of activity
senses.definition: full of people, movement and excitement, as a place or an event
senses.definitionCN: 充满人群、动静与兴奋感，用来形容地方或活动
senses.example: The square becomes lively after the shops close.
senses.exampleCN: 商店打烊之后，广场就热闹起来。
senses.why: A crowd moves and makes noise like one large body; a place that will not stay quiet borrows the same word.
senses.whyCN: 人群又动又响，像一个巨大的身体；一个安静不下来的地方就借用了同一个词。

senses.title: Bright and strong in colour
senses.definition: of colour, bright and strong enough to catch the eye immediately
senses.definitionCN: 指颜色明亮强烈，一眼就能抓住视线
senses.example: The walls were painted a lively shade of orange.
senses.exampleCN: 墙壁被刷成一种鲜艳的橙色。
senses.why: Strong colour jumps at the eye the way a moving body does; the visual shock is read as a sign of life.
senses.whyCN: 浓烈的颜色像活动的身体一样跳进眼里；这种视觉冲击被读成生命力的标志。

senses.title: Vigorous and full of argument
senses.definition: of a discussion, debate or game, energetic and full of strong, differing views
senses.definitionCN: 指讨论、辩论或比赛充满劲头，带着强烈而不同的意见
senses.example: The proposal led to a lively debate in the council.
senses.exampleCN: 这项提议在议事会里引发了一场激烈的辩论。
senses.why: A debate that keeps returning and refuses to settle behaves like a restless creature; the energy of life is lent to argument.
senses.whyCN: 一场反复回到原点、不肯定论的辩论，举止就像一个停不下来的活物；生命的劲头被借给了争论。

intro.en: Lively began as a Germanic compound meaning life-like, and it gradually shifted from living creatures to vivid speech, bright colour and busy places.
intro.cn: lively 最初是一个意为「像生命一样的」日耳曼语复合词，后来逐渐从活物转到生动的言语、鲜亮的颜色和热闹的地方。

items.en: Old English liflic meant living or having life, built from lif, life, and the suffix -lic.
items.cn: 古英语 liflic 意为有生命的、活着的，由 lif（生命）与后缀 -lic 构成。

items.en: The noun is reconstructed as libam, the ancestor of life; the suffix -lic is related to German -lich and English -ly.
items.cn: 这个词的名词部分一般重构为 libam，是 life 的祖先；后缀 -lic 与德语 -lich、英语 -ly 同源。

items.en: Middle English lively kept the sense living and began to mean active, quick and cheerful.
items.cn: 中古英语的 lively 保留了「活着的」义项，并开始表示活跃、轻快、快活。

items.en: By the sixteenth century lively could describe vivid speech, bright colour and busy places, not only living creatures.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，lively 已能形容生动的言辞、鲜亮的颜色和热闹的地方，不再只用于活物。

items.en: Modern English uses lively mainly for energy and vividness; the older sense of living survives in a few fixed phrases such as a lively hope.
items.cn: 现代英语的 lively 主要用于表示活力与生动；较旧的「活着的」义项只留在少数固定说法里，如 a lively hope。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Germanic word for life; the near-meaning group gathers words for energy, vividness and busy activity.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在日耳曼语「生命」一词上的词；近义组收表示精力、生动与忙碌活动的词。

entries.definition: The quality of being lively.
entries.definitionCN: 活泼；生动；由 lively 加 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: To be alive, or to spend one's life in a place.
entries.definitionCN: 活着；居住；与 lively 同源。

entries.definition: The state of being alive.
entries.definitionCN: 生命；活着的状态；与 lively 同源。

entries.definition: Living, not dead.
entries.definitionCN: 活着的；未死的；与 lively 同源。

entries.definition: Full of energy and ready to act.
entries.definitionCN: 精力充沛的；随时准备行动的。

entries.definition: Producing a strong, clear picture in the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 生动的；在脑中形成鲜明画面的。

entries.definition: Full of busy movement and noise.
entries.definitionCN: 熙熙攘攘的；充满忙碌动静与喧闹的。

entries.definition: Happy and positive in mood.
entries.definitionCN: 快活的；情绪愉快积极的。

normalIntro.en: The word joins the Germanic noun for life to a suffix of likeness, and its family keeps returning to living energy and vivid movement.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把日耳曼语中表示「生命」的名词与表示「像……一样」的后缀结合起来，同族词反复回到活着的劲头与生动的动感。

normal.en: Old English liflic is life plus -lic, the suffix that became -ly; lively literally means life-like.
normal.cn: 古英语 liflic 是 life 加 -lic，也就是后来变成 -ly 的那个后缀；lively 字面上就是「像生命一样的」。

normal.en: The same suffix -ly appears in friendly and lovely, turning nouns into adjectives about a quality.
normal.cn: 同一个后缀 -ly 也出现在 friendly 与 lovely 里，把名词变成表示某种性质的形容词。

normal.en: Life, live and alive are close relatives, so a lively room is a room that seems to be alive.
normal.cn: life、live 与 alive 是近亲，所以一间 lively 的屋子就像一间活着的屋子。

normal.en: The word first described a living, moving body, and only later described speech, colour and markets.
normal.cn: 这个词最早描述会动会叫的活物，后来才用来描述言语、颜色和市场。

normal.en: Liveliness adds -ness to lively, naming the quality that a lively person or place shows.
normal.cn: liveliness 在 lively 后加 -ness，用来指活泼的人或地方所表现出的那种性质。

abstract.en: A lively room is one that behaves like a body: it moves, makes sound and will not sit still.
abstract.cn: 一间 lively 的屋子举止像个身体：会动、会响、不肯安静。

abstract.en: We call a description lively when reading it feels like watching something happen.
abstract.cn: 我们把一段描写称作 lively，是因为读它时像在看事情发生。

abstract.en: Bright colour and heated debate share the word because both refuse to stay quiet.
abstract.cn: 鲜艳的颜色与激烈的辩论共用这个词，因为两者都不肯安静。

examples.en: The lively children kept the whole street awake with their shouting.
examples.cn: 这些活泼的孩子用喊声让整条街都醒着。

examples.en: She gave a lively account of the market on a rainy morning.
examples.cn: 她把雨中清晨的集市讲得活灵活现。

examples.en: The square becomes lively after the shops close.
examples.cn: 商店打烊之后，广场就热闹起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来福里」——家里来了福气，人人有说有笑，日子过得很活泼；lively 是活泼的、生动的。

root: 古英语 liflic（有生命的）＝ lif（生命）＋ -lic（……样的，后演变为 -ly）；与 life、live、alive 同源，属日耳曼语族，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is living energy; the senses divide into the energetic person, the vivid description, the busy place, the bright colour and the heated debate.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是活着的劲头；义项由此分出精力充沛的人、生动的描写、热闹的地方、鲜艳的颜色与激烈的辩论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: children chasing a ball across a yard, their shouting lifting the quiet afternoon.
core.cn: 核心意象：孩子们在院子里追着皮球跑，喊声把安静的午后掀了起来。

branches.en: children running and shouting across a yard
branches.cn: 孩子们在院子里奔跑喊叫

branches.en: a market square filling with voices at dusk
branches.cn: 黄昏时集市广场人声渐满

branches.en: a storyteller making a rainy morning come alive
branches.cn: 讲故事的人把雨晨说得活灵活现

branches.en: a wall painted a strong orange
a council chamber ringing with argument

intro.en: A Germanic noun for life, a suffix of likeness, one Old English adjective and two English suffixes carry lively from a moving body to vivid speech and busy streets.
intro.cn: 一个日耳曼语的生命名词、一个表示「像……一样」的后缀、一个古英语形容词，再加两个英语后缀，把 lively 从活动的身体带到生动的言语与热闹的街道。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; lively belongs to a Germanic family built on the word for life.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；lively 属于建立在「生命」一词之上的日耳曼语族。

definition_zh: 未来；将来；前途；（语法）将来时；期货
definition_en: the time that will come after now, or what will happen or be possible later
core_image: 一条从脚下伸向雾中的长路，路灯一盏盏亮向远方
scene: 毕业典礼结束，学生们把学士帽抛向天空。 Every graduate faced the future with both excitement and a little fear.
sceneCN: 这里 future 是「未来」（第 1 个义项：此刻之后的时间）；句意为每位毕业生都怀着兴奋与些许不安面对未来。

derivatives.zh: future 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「未来性；将来之事」
future 加 -ism 构成，义为「未来主义」

senses.title: The time to come
senses.definition: the period of time that will come after the present
senses.definitionCN: 现在之后将要到来的时间段
senses.example: No one can predict the future with certainty.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人能准确预测未来。
senses.why: The word names the whole of time ahead of us, the base direction sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名我们前方的时间整体，是基础的方向性义项。

senses.title: Prospects or likely success
senses.definition: the chances or prospects awaiting a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某物等待其去把握的机会或前景
senses.example: She has a bright future in medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 她在医学领域前途光明。
senses.why: The road ahead is read as the fate ahead, so personal prospects borrow the time image.
senses.whyCN: 前方的路被解读为前方的命运，个人前途借用了时间画面。

senses.title: Grammar form for later time
senses.definition: the verb form used to talk about actions after now
senses.definitionCN: 用于谈论现在之后动作的动词形式
senses.example: English marks the future with will or shall.
senses.exampleCN: 英语用 will 或 shall 标记将来。
senses.why: Language packages time into forms, so the time-ahead sense becomes a grammar label.
senses.whyCN: 语言把时间打包成形式，于是「将来」义成为语法标签。

senses.title: Contracts bought for later delivery
senses.definition: agreements to buy or sell goods at set prices on a later date
senses.definitionCN: 约定在日后按定价交割货物的合约
senses.example: Traders bought coffee futures to hedge prices.
senses.exampleCN: 交易商买入咖啡期货对冲价格。
senses.why: Dealing in tomorrow's goods keeps the ahead-of-time idea inside finance.
senses.whyCN: 交易明天的货物，把「 ahead of time」的观念留在金融领域。

senses.title: Coming after the present
senses.definition: happening or existing after now, used before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 发生在现在之后，用于名词前
senses.example: Future meetings will be shorter.
senses.exampleCN: 以后的会议会开得更短。
senses.why: The noun slides into the adjective slot to mark anything belonging to later time.
senses.whyCN: 名词滑入形容词位置，标记一切属于将来的事物。

senses.title: Later holders of a role
senses.definition: someone who will hold a position or status later
senses.definitionCN: 日后将担任某职位或拥有某身份的人
senses.example: the future king greeted the crowd
senses.exampleCN: 未来的国王向人群致意
senses.why: A person's later status is described with the time word fixed before the title.
senses.whyCN: 把时间词固定放在头衔前，即可描述一个人日后的身份。

intro.en: Future descends from Latin futurus, the participle of a verb meaning to be about to be.
intro.cn: future 源自拉丁语 futurus，即意为「将要存在」的动词的分词。

items.en: Latin esse meant to be, and its future participle futurus meant about to be.
items.cn: 拉丁语 esse 意为「存在」，其将来分词 futurus 意为「将要存在的」。

items.en: The stem fu- is an irregular suppletive form of the verb to be.
items.cn: 词干 fu- 是动词 be 的不规则异干替代形式。

items.en: Futurus came to act as a noun, futura, for things to come.
items.cn: futurus 后来名词化为 futura，指将要来临之事。

items.en: Middle English took future from Old French in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 中古英语十四世纪经古法语借入 future。

items.en: Modern English spread it into grammar, finance, and everyday hope-talk.

definition_zh: 职员；店员；办事员；文书
definition_en: a person who works in an office or shop keeping records or serving customers
core_image: 柜台后或办公桌前，一边整理文件一边招呼客人的人
scene: 超市里，收银员正帮妈妈扫码结账。 The clerk scanned the food quickly at the supermarket.
sceneCN: 这里 clerk 是「店员」（第 1 个义项：在商店里服务顾客的人）；句意是超市店员麻利地给食物扫码。

senses.title: A worker serving customers in a shop
senses.definition: a person whose job is to serve customers in a store
senses.definitionCN: 在商店里为顾客服务的人
senses.example: The clerk helped me find the right size of shoes.
senses.exampleCN: 店员帮我找到了合适尺码的鞋子。
senses.why: Shops need someone standing behind the counter to hand goods over, so the person doing that job got this name.
senses.whyCN: 商店需要有人站在柜台后递出商品，做这份工作的人便得到了这个称呼。

senses.title: An office worker keeping records
senses.definition: a person who keeps records and accounts in an office
senses.definitionCN: 在办公室里保管记录和账目的人
senses.example: The clerk filed all the letters in the big cabinet.
senses.exampleCN: 职员把所有信件都归档进大柜子里。
senses.why: Offices run on papers and lists, and the worker who handles them daily became known as the clerk.
senses.whyCN: 办公室靠文件和清单运转，每天处理这些文件的工人就成了 clerk。

senses.title: An official who keeps records for a court or town
senses.definition: an official who keeps records for a court, a town or a club
senses.definitionCN: 为法庭、城镇或社团保管记录的公务人员
senses.example: The court clerk read out the case number.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭书记员念出了案件编号。
senses.why: Because record-keeping was once done by church-trained men, the official sense grew out of the clerical one.

intro.en: Clerk and cleric are twins: the word began as a title for churchmen.
intro.cn: clerk 与 cleric 是双胞胎：这个词最初是教士的头衔。

items.en: Greek kleros meant a lot or share of land, later the clergy as God's share.
items.cn: 希腊语 kleros 本指抽签分得的份地，后来指「属于上帝的一份」即教士。

items.en: Late Latin clericus meant a clergyman, a man who could read and write.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 clericus 指教士，即识字、能读写的人。

items.en: Old English cleric borrowed the word for churchmen, the few people who kept records.
items.cn: 古英语借入 cleric 一词称呼教士——当时少数会做记录的人。

items.en: Old French clerc passed the word on with both the church sense and the writer sense.
items.cn: 古法语 clerc 把「教士」和「写字人」两层意思一并传了过来。

items.en: Middle English clerk slowly shifted from holy men to paid record-keepers and shop workers.
items.cn: 中古英语 clerk 渐渐从神职人员转指拿工资的记录员和店员。

items.en: Modern English kept the spelling but split the sound: British /klɑːk/, American /klɜːrk/.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了拼写但读音分了家：英式 /klɑːk/，美式 /klɜːrk/。

note.en: The first group collects words that look or sound close to clerk; the second collects people who work in offices and shops.

definition_zh: 还；仍然；（用于否定）尚未；然而；但是
definition_en: up to now, or still, used mostly in questions and negatives, and also as a word of contrast
core_image: 钟表停在原地，指针还没往前挪，但随时可以挪
scene: 饭桌上菜都摆好了，最后一个人还没到，大家就先把碗筷放下等着。 The soup is not ready yet, so please sit down for a moment.
sceneCN: 这里 yet 是「尚未」（第 2 个义项：用在否定句中表示到现在还没发生）；句意为汤还没好，请坐一会儿。钟表停在原地还没往前挪，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 同源方言名词，义为「大门」，与 yet 的副词用法无关
固定说法，义为「到目前为止」

senses.title: Still going on
senses.definition: used to say that something is still true or still continuing at the present time
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事到此刻仍然如此或仍在继续
senses.example: There is yet time to change the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 还有时间改计划。
senses.why: The oldest sense meant still or up to now, and that meaning sits inside every later use.
senses.whyCN: 最早的意思是「仍然、直到现在」，这个意思藏在后来每一种用法里。

senses.title: Not up to now
senses.definition: used in negative sentences or questions to say that something has not happened up to now
senses.definitionCN: 用于否定句或疑问句，表示到现在还没发生
senses.example: The soup is not ready yet, so please sit down for a moment.
senses.exampleCN: 汤还没好，请坐一会儿。
senses.why: If the word marks the time up to now, then in a negative sentence it marks the point that has not been reached.
senses.whyCN: 如果这个词标的是「直到现在」，那么放在否定句里它标的就是尚未到达的那一点。

senses.title: The word of contrast
senses.definition: used as a conjunction to introduce something that contrasts with what was just said
senses.definitionCN: 作连词，引出与上文形成对照的内容
senses.example: The room was small, yet it felt comfortable.
senses.exampleCN: 房间很小，然而很舒服。
senses.why: The step from still to however is short: what is still true can quietly contradict what was just claimed.
senses.whyCN: 从「仍然」到「然而」只隔一步：仍然成立的事，可以悄悄推翻刚刚说过的话。

senses.title: One more time
senses.definition: used before again or another to show that something is repeated, often with mild annoyance
senses.definitionCN: 用在 again 或 another 前表示重复，常带一点不耐烦
senses.example: He was late yet again this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 今早他又一次迟到了。
senses.why: Repetition is just duration continued, so the word of still also marks another round of the same thing.
senses.whyCN: 重复不过是持续下去，所以「仍然」这个词也能标出同样事情又来一轮。

senses.title: The best so far
senses.definition: used after a superlative to mean up to this time
senses.definitionCN: 用在最高级后，表示到现在为止
senses.example: This is her best film yet.
senses.exampleCN: 这是她至今最好的一部电影。
senses.why: Because the word marks the limit of time up to now, a superlative with yet means the record so far.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词标的是时间的上限，所以与最高级连用就表示「到目前为止」的纪录。

intro.en: Yet comes from an Old English word meaning still or up to now, and the conjunction use grew out of that adverb.
intro.cn: yet 出自古英语中意为「仍然、直到现在」的词，连词用法由这个副词长出来。

items.en: The root carried the idea of something continuing up to a point, shared with Dutch and German relatives.
items.cn: 这个词根带有「一直持续到某点」的意思，与荷兰语、德语亲属词共有。

items.en: giet and gīet meant still, or up to this time, in both prose and poetry.
items.cn: 古英语 giet、gīet 在散文与诗歌中都意为「仍然、直到此时」。

items.en: The form shortened to yet, and the negative pattern not yet became common.
items.cn: 形式简化为 yet，否定结构 not yet 变得常用。

items.en: The contrastive use as a conjunction spread in written prose.
items.cn: 作连词表示转折的用法在书面散文中流行起来。

items.en: Uses with comparatives and superlatives settled, giving the best yet and yet again.
items.cn: 与比较级、最高级连用的用法固定下来，产生了 the best yet、yet again。

note.cn: yet 在拼写上接近几个短词，在意思上接近其他时间词与转折词。

normalIntro.cn: yet 标的是「直到现在」这条线，各个义项要么延续它，要么把它变成转折。

normal.en: Not yet is the most common pattern, because the word lives in the gap before something happens.
normal.cn: not yet 是最常见的搭配，因为这个词就住在事情发生前的空档里。

normal.en: Have yet to do something means the same as have not done it so far.
normal.cn: have yet to do 与「到现在还没做」意思相同。

normal.en: As yet means up to this point, and it keeps the pure time meaning.
normal.cn: as yet 意为「到目前为止」，保留了纯粹的时间义。

normal.en: In the sentence the room was small, yet comfortable, the word simply turns the line back.
normal.cn: 在「房间小，然而舒服」这句里，这个词只是把话拐了一个弯。
